findings.detail: the release lands on ms-quantized AudioContext times, so runs repeat splice positions (CONT-1: 4 distinct `when` values in 6 runs; CONT-30: 2 distinct values, 5 of 6 runs identical in every reported field incl. contiguity [-2967, 550.8] ms at when 2.9902). The first run of each set differs, so nothing is replayed from disk; the identical runs fit a deterministic headless audio sink rendering the same stem at the same splice position, but the probe saves no raw captures, so C cannot exclude a stale capture after the fact. B's own runs show the same pattern (5/6 at 2.9815). Not a FAIL (validity rule met, the PASS is defined by the click rule). For the future replace-splice probe: add a random pre-release delay and save the raw captures

C experiment outside the rows: a positive control (a hard Stop during playback through the same tap, c-round-308/posctl-probe.cjs) could not show the click rule's sensitivity, because Stop disconnects the tapped nodes and the capture ends at the stop (splicedInCapture false, contiguous span [-2569, 0] ms). The probe's ability to flag a real splice discontinuity therefore remains unproven in the browser; the CONT PASS rests on the rule as B specified it. A future replace-splice probe (doc 224 TODO) should include a positive control, e.g. a deliberately unfaded restart
